methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a two-center retrospective design with 177 internal and 83 external patients, appropriate feature reduction (ICC>0.75, mRMR, LASSO with 10-fold CV), and three ML classifiers with 5-fold hyperparameter tuning. The authors explicitly report 5-fold cross-validation results (LR AUC 0.835 ± 0.055) alongside held-out validation and external validation, and employ DeLong's test for ROC comparisons. Limitations include retrospective design, single-institution training data, exclusion of clinical variables for parsimony, and no prospective validation, which the authors acknowledge. Sample size is modest for a radiomics study, slightly limiting rigor.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The task (distinguishing IAC from pre-invasive SSNs <1cm) has direct clinical utility for surgical planning and surveillance decisions, and DCA demonstrates net benefit over treat-all/treat-none. However, as a two-center retrospective prediction model without prospective deployment or impact assessment, translational relevance is plausible but not demonstrated. The design is a retrospective cohort/case series of surgical patients, mapping to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort/case series of prognostic/diagnostic accuracy type).

reporting_quality.justification: As a prediction-model development and external validation study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard; the paper reports cohort definitions, predictors, feature selection, model development, performance metrics (discrimination, calibration, DCA), and external validation. However, there is no explicit TRIPOD checklist, limited reporting of missing data handling, no sample size justification, and the Radiomics Quality Score is invoked only via a supplementary table. Data and code availability are not mentioned beyond a proprietary uAI platform, yielding a low reproducibility score.

novelty_literature.justification: Radiomics-ML pipelines for lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness prediction are a well-established area, with the authors explicitly citing Zuo et al. and Li et al. doing highly similar work. The paper's incremental contributions are restricting to subcentimeter SSNs and emphasizing SHAP interpretability, both of which are modest extensions rather than novel methodology. SHAP use in radiomics is now common, and performance (AUC 0.842/0.778) is comparable to prior models. The study confirms rather than redefines the field.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a clear IMRaD structure, comprehensive tables and figures, and adequate explanations of SHAP-derived features. Weaknesses include duplicated sentences in the ROI extraction section (the PyRadiomics/IBSI description appears twice), inconsistent figure referencing (Figure 8 described both for external validation and SHAP; Figure 9 similarly confused), a typo 'bees warm' for 'beeswarm', and two 'Third' limitations items. Writing is adequate but needs careful copyediting.

key_strengths: Inclusion of an independent external validation cohort from a second hospital with matched scanner hardware
Rigorous feature stability screening (ICC>0.75) combined with mRMR and LASSO selection
DeLong's test and 5-fold cross-validation used to justify model selection and address overfitting concerns
SHAP-based global and local interpretability with biologically plausible feature narratives
Decision curve analysis included to quantify clinical net benefit
key_concerns: Novelty is limited; highly similar radiomics+SHAP lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness models already exist (Zuo, Li)
Sample sizes (177 internal, 83 external) are modest for a 10-feature model predicting a ~45% prevalence outcome
No reporting standard (TRIPOD) checklist, no sample-size calculation, and proprietary uAI platform limits reproducibility
Clinical variables excluded, so the model cannot be compared head-to-head with clinico-radiomic nomograms
Duplicated text and confused figure numbering reflect insufficient copyediting
Retrospective single-training-site design leaves residual selection and scanner bias despite hardware matching
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent but incremental radiomics-ML prediction study with modest sample size, limited novelty, and reproducibility gaps; best fits a Tier 3 specialty journal after major revisions.
